He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse Orange]], [[Seton Hall Pirates men's basketball|Seton Hall Pirates]] and [[St. John's Red Storm men's basketball|St. John's Red Storm]]. ==High school career== Richmond played for [[Midwood High School]] in his hometown of [[Brooklyn]] as a freshman before transferring to [[South Shore High School (Brooklyn)|South Shore High School]].{{cite web |last=Dabbundo |first=Anthony |title=How Kadary Richmond's past paved his way to Syracuse |url=http://dailyorange.com/2021/02/kadary-richmonds-past-paved-way-syracuse/ |website=[[The Daily Orange]] |access-date=May 25, 2021 |date=February 14, 2021}} He helped South Shore win two [[Public Schools Athletic League]] Class AA titles.{{cite web |last=Cordova |first=David |title=This Is New York: Part 9: Kadary Richmond Has A Big Summer |url=https://davesjoint.net/2019/08/22/this-is-new-york-part-9-kadary-richmond-has-a-big-summer/ |website=Dave's Joint |access-date=May 25, 2021 |date=August 22, 2019}} Richmond played a [[postgraduate season]] at [[Brewster Academy]] in [[Wolfeboro, New Hampshire]].{{cite web |last=Gutierrez |first=Matthew |title=His dream realized, Syracuse's Kadary Richmond is ready to work |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1904169/2020/07/02/his-dream-realized-syracuses-kadary-richmond-is-ready-to-work/ |website=[[The Athletic]] |access-date=May 25, 2021 |date=July 2, 2020}} He averaged 12.5 points, six rebounds and 3.8 assists per game, receiving First Team All-[[New England Preparatory School Athletic Council]] Class AAA honors.{{cite web |last=Ditota |first=Donna |title=News on 6-foot-7 point guard Kadary Richmond, a 'nice get' for Syracuse basketball |url=https://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/2020/03/news-on-6-foot-7-point-guard-kadary-richmond-a-nice-get-for-syracuse-basketball.html |website=[[The Post-Standard]] |access-date=May 25, 2021 |date=March 18, 2020}} A four-star recruit, Richmond committed to playing college basketball for [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]] over offers from [[UConn Huskies men's basketball|UConn]], [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]], [[Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball|Cincinnati]] and [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown]].{{cite web |last=Dabbundo |first=Anthony |title=4-star combo guard Kadary Richmond commits to Syracuse |url=http://dailyorange.com/2019/10/4-star-combo-guard-kadary-richmond-commits-syracuse/ |website=[[The Daily Orange]] |access-date=May 25, 2021 |date=October 28, 2019}} ==College career== ===Syracuse Orange=== On December 3, 2020, Richmond made his first career start for Syracuse in the absence of [[Buddy Boeheim]]. He recorded a freshman season-high 16 points, seven rebounds, six assists, four steals and three blocks in a 75–45 win over [[Niagara Purple Eagles men's basketball|Niagara]].{{cite web |last=McAllister |first=Mike |title=Richmond Puts Together Stellar Performance in First Start |url=https://www.si.com/college/syracuse/basketball/kadary-richmond-stellar-performance-first-start-niagara |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=May 25, 2021 |date=December 3, 2020}} As a freshman, he averaged 6.3 points, 3.1 assists, 2.6 rebounds and 1.6 steals in 21 minutes per game.{{cite web |last=Adler |first=Neil |title=Syracuse Basketball: Kadary Richmond will have big list of big-time suitors |url=https://insidetheloudhouse.com/2021/03/31/syracuse-basketball-kadary-richmond-will-big-list-big-time-suitors/ |website=Inside the Loud House |access-date=May 25, 2021 |date=March 31, 2021}} ===Seton Hall Pirates=== After the season, Richmond transferred to [[Seton Hall Pirates men's basketball|Seton Hall]].{{cite web |last=Carino |first=Jerry |title=Seton Hall basketball adds Syracuse transfer Kadary Richmond |url=https://www.app.com/story/sports/college/2021/04/06/seton-hall-basketball-adds-syracuse-transfer-kadary-richmond/7110000002/ |website=[[Asbury Park Press]] |access-date=May 25, 2021 |date=April 6, 2021}} On January 8, 2022, he scored a career-high 27 points in a 90-87 overtime win over [[UConn Huskies men's basketball|UConn]].{{cite news |last=Zagoria |first=Adam |title=Kadary Richmond, Bryce Aiken combine for 49 points as No. 24 Seton Hall outlasts UConn in overtime |url=https://www.nj.com/setonhall/2022/01/kadary-richmond-bryce-aiken-combine-for-49-points-as-no-24-seton-hall-outlasts-uconn-in-overtime.html |access-date=January 8, 2022 |work=[[NJ.com]] |date=January 8, 2022}} Richmond began playing more minutes later in January 2022 due to [[Bryce Aiken]] being in concussion protocol, and coach [[Kevin Willard]] said of Richmond, "I think you're starting to see the evolution of a really, really good player."{{cite news |last=Zagoria |first=Adam |title=With Bryce Aiken sidelined, Kadary Richmond is making steady progress as Seton Hall's point guard |url=https://www.nj.com/setonhall/2022/02/with-bryce-aiken-sidelined-kadary-richmond-is-making-steady-progress-as-seton-halls-point-guard.html |access-date=February 7, 2022 |work=[[NJ.com]] |date=February 6, 2022}} As a senior, Richmond earned first-team All-[[Big East]] honors after averaging 15.7 points, 7.0 rebounds and 5.1 assists per game. He led Seton Hall to an NIT title, contributing 21 points, 13 rebounds in the championship game against [[Indiana State Sycamores men's basketball|Indiana State]].{{cite news |last=Borzello |first=Jeff |title=Seton Hall star Kadary Richmond enters transfer portal |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/40025291 |access-date=February 6, 2025 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=April 25, 2024}} ===St. John's Red Storm=== In May 2024, Richmond transferred to [[St. John's Red Storm men's basketball|St. John's]] to play for [[Rick Pitino]].{{cite news |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |last2=Borzello |first2=Jeff |title=Kadary Richmond transfers from Seton Hall to St. John's |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/40101374 |access-date=February 6, 2025 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=May 7, 2024|name-list-style=and}} ==Professional career== Following the close of his college career, Richmond signed with the [[Capital City Go-Go]] of the [[NBA G League]]. On February 11, 2026, Richmond was signed to a 10-day contract by the [[Washington Wizards]], and debuted for the team that evening.{{cite web |last1=Mawby |first1=Zachary |title=Former men’s basketball star guard makes NBA debut with Wizards |url=https://www.thesetonian.com/article/2026/02/former-mens-basketball-star-guard-makes-nba-debut-with-wizards |website=The Setonian |access-date=April 7, 2026 |date=February 12, 2026}} He appeared in three NBA games, before his 10-day contract expired, and he returned to the Go-Go. ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics
